summary: Module 3 VERIFY answers. (1) Trigger variable: Concurrency. The other two candidates were eliminated: Data -- the repro used ordinary, freshly-created links with no special metadata or edge-case slugs, and single-request runs of those same links never errored; Timing -- the failure window is the check-then-act gap, not a wall-clock rollover, and forced-identical candidate repro fired two requests within milliseconds on the same bucket. Concurrency confirmed by a deterministic repro: two creators computing the SAME candidate before either INSERT commits produced 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint links_code_key' -- the exact failure class in the module's log line. (2) A single curl would never have found it: sequential requests always observe the row that exists, so the SELECT-then-INSERT window never overlaps; only concurrent arrival opens it. That is the gap between 'I tested it' (proves one happy path) and 'I tested it thoroughly' (exercises interleavings). (3) Same race class audit: concurrent writes in this fork are (a) click recording -- already atomic (single INSERT + unique event_key + IntegrityError skip, no pre-SELECT); (b) link creation -- was SELECT-then-INSERT on unique links.code, now fixed; (c) cache writes via Redis set (atomic single op); (d) rate-limit counters via Redis INCR (atomic). No other SELECT-then-INSERT write paths remain. (4) Why 10: with 2, the race window opens but probability of the exact interleave is tiny, so failures are flaky; 10 raises collision probability sharply and exposes the bug in a few runs; 1000 would hammer rate limits (120 redirects/min) and produce 429s, confounding the signal. There is no reliable minimum that triggers the flaky window -- that is exactly why a deterministic repro (forced identical candidate) matters more than cranking concurrency; and why in production the bug surfaces only on popular links where burst concurrency overlaps the window.
